memo.verdict: Neutral; park. The record recommends parking Xvivo (XVIVO-SE) at 240.0 SEK (2026-09-22) pending two dated events within five weeks: the European CE-mark decision on the heart preservation solution (feedback was expected during Q3 2026; no file in the folder records the outcome; the record takes no view on it) and the Q3 2026 report on 22 October 2026. Conviction: a working hypothesis. The park rule does not trigger by its own terms (management C, business quality C, predictability C, trackability C); the park is a judgement on the return against the risk. Entry level: about 230 SEK, the price below which the case clears the 20 percent bar on both horizons on our path (4 percent below today's price). What moves it to bullish and progress: a CE mark in hand and a Q3 report with lung disposables above 30 percent and services no worse, at a price at or below 230 SEK; or any price below about 200 SEK without a change in the case (a 25 percent-plus return on our path). What moves it to bearish: lung disposables below 20 percent for two quarters; an FDA request for further heart data; an abdominal gross margin below 60 percent after the consolidation. The case is not invalidated: the growth engine is accelerating, the balance sheet is net cash, the drivers are few and the resolving events are dated and near.
case: The thesis: Xvivo is a demand-inflection case with one proven engine and three unproven ones; the lung consumables business is real and accelerating, the heart system is the prize, the regulator holds the key; at 240 SEK the shares already pay for the prize on the sell-side's timetable, so on our slower path the modal return reaches the 20 percent bar only at three years and only if the multiple holds.

The change is external, structural and sector-wide. Machine perfusion is being pulled into transplant practice by forces independent of Xvivo: circulatory-death donors near a 50/50 split with brain-death donors in the US in 2025, growing over 7 percent a year, and such organs need perfusion to be assessed; 55.8 percent of US circulatory-death donors underwent normothermic regional perfusion in Q1 2026; underperforming procurement organisations face decertification by 2026 with administrative actions begun (the HRSA review temporarily weighed on US lung and kidney sales); every player is growing (TransMedics +37 percent in 2025 to USD 605.5m; OrganOx +50 percent under Terumo; Paragonix +65 percent organic under Getinge); demand for transplantable organs is ten times supply. Transplant procedures grow only 5 to 7 percent a year (market 7 percent a year to USD 2.9bn by 2033), so the inflection is in perfusion penetration (US lung EVLP about 10 percent; machine perfusion 4 percent of the market), capped by cost at 10 to 20 percent of US lung transplants on expert testimony (USD 40,000 a run). External forces B: three tailwinds (donor mix; procurement reform; sector adoption) against two headwinds, competition D (Terumo bought OrganOx for about USD 1.5bn in October 2025 targeting 25 percent a year growth to about 100 billion yen; Getinge bought Paragonix for USD 477m in September 2024; Bridge to Life's VitaSmart FDA De Novo January 2026 at USD 15,000 to 20,000 a case; TransMedics' CHOPS into cold storage; United Therapeutics' CLES and Traferox's TorEx against the XPS in lung; rivals from one to four in two years; the sell-side's base rate that three-plus well-funded competitors compress EBITDA margins below 20 percent within five years) and macro D (USD about 55 percent and EUR about 35 percent of sales against a SEK cost base, zero hedging, consensus USD/SEK 9.70 to 9.15 by end-2026 and 8.67 by late 2027; a 10 percent move costs about 45 SEKm of sales and 0.36 SEK of EPS; over 76 percent of surveyed hospital executives cap capital spending). Own cycle A (turned Q4 2025, accelerated through H1 2026; non-cyclical demand; the cycle is the company's destocking and launch timing). Political and regulatory B (decertification; French national reimbursement for the heart technology 18 May 2026 ahead of CE mark; Health Canada approvals; CMS cost recovery; against, the CE mark six to twelve months late and the DeLIVER trial paused pending a de novo pathway; tariffs modest because nearly 50 percent of sales are US-made lung consumables). Disruption B (xenotransplantation and cryopreservation ten to fifteen years away and needing perfusion; United Therapeutics' EXPRESS pig-heart trial cleared May 2026 with Xvivo's fluids in both first US pig-to-human transplants; the live disruptor is customer insourcing). Supply C (outsourced to a small Western network, no volume discounts, savings take twelve to eighteen months, Dextran 40 dependency, the XPS shortage resolved late 2025).

The company's own change is an execution programme riding that demand, not a transformation (internal forces C: meets the framework's "at least three strong" only at the margin; no chief-executive change since November 2022; no numerical guidance; red flags absent). New products A: the heart system live in Europe under derogation (24 SEKm in Q2 2026 against 3 SEKm) and in the US under a continued-access protocol expanded by 60 patients on 3 August 2026, PMA submission planned shortly after summer 2026; Kidney Assist Transport launched in Canada, broader US launch 2027; at layer 3 of the chain for the US. Strategy B: device vendor to integrated service and logistics partner (the "10x value" of a perfusion run), resourced (Perfusion Solution Inc's 175 perfusionists; MTJ Aviation; three OPO hubs against a four-to-five target), producing output in lung and failing in organ recovery services (-25 percent organic; a former director calls US service execution "terrible"). Gothenburg consolidation B (finishing Q4 2026; unit-cost benefits from 2027; the force behind the abdominal margin leg). Standards B (H2 2025 cost and cash programme: record 25 percent adjusted EBITDA margin Q4 2025, two cash-positive quarters; rolling forecasts; US field force restructured summer 2026; 12 percent a year perfusion-volume growth in the incentive plan; against, eNPS 51 to 27). New geographies B (Canada; France; Australia and Europe under derogation; US South and West Coast). Other leaders C (the finance director's redeployment, the vacancy the leadership report calls the single most important execution risk over twelve months; two new directors 27 April 2026). Guidance C (2027 targets: EBITDA margin over 30 percent, EBIT margin over 20 percent, abdominal gross margin 70 percent, reaffirmed not raised 14 July 2026; FY2026 EBITDA in line with consensus; ambitious against a 19 percent Q2 2026 margin). Price rises C (disposable margins held at 84 percent in 2023; abdominal price fell in 2026 on emerging-market kidney mix; STEEN at about USD 7,000 a litre). Chief executive C, balance sheet C (capitalised development 153 SEKm in 2025; consensus capex 200 SEKm; EUR 20m facility drawn EUR 8m; net cash 183 SEKm), acquisitions C (phase over; Organ Assist 2020, STAR Teams 2021, Avionord 2022, FlowHawk late 2024 for 57 SEKm; acquired growth 1 percent in 2025), perimeter C, shareholder returns D (zero dividend; no buyback).
counter_case: Xvivo is a false friend: a science company with a superb lung consumables franchise whose revenue acceleration in 2026 is a rebound from a destocked 2025 (two-year stacked growth of about 16 percent a year), dressed up by the accounting (152.8 SEKm of development capitalised in 2025, 19 percent of sales, against 20.1 SEKm amortised; 800.7 SEKm deferred; free cash flow 7.3 SEKm in FY2025 and -4 SEKm in Q2 2026 while EBITDA prints a 19 to 25 percent margin, so the 20 percent EBITDA margin is flattered and cash EBITDA is roughly 130 SEKm lower than reported), and undermined below the surface by a services unit a former director calls terrible (-25 percent organic; 10 percent gross margin from 34), an abdominal gross margin that fell from 68 to 57 percent in a year on the very mix (kidney; emerging markets) the growth plan requires, an unhedged currency exposure of about 90 percent of revenue into a krona consensus macro expects to strengthen (USD/SEK to 8.67 by late 2027; a 10 percent move costs 45 SEKm of sales and 0.36 SEK of EPS; a simultaneous 30 percent fall in USD and EUR removes 220 SEKm of revenue and 79 SEKm of EBITDA), and a regulatory record in which every date has slipped (the CE mark by six to twelve months; PRESERVE by 60 added patients; DeLIVER paused). Its largest customer (over 10 percent of revenue; 132 SEKm in 2025; the destocker that produced a -15 percent quarter and a 30 percent one-day share fall) is building its own lung-evaluation system. Its heart product enters a market where TransMedics has over 1,000 US cases and an integrated aviation network of 21 aircraft, and where TransMedics says cold perfusion "causes ischaemic damage" and the hypothermic box cannot show real-time organ function. Its liver product will face Terumo's OrganOx (growing 50 percent, FDA transport approval) and Bridge to Life at USD 15,000 to 20,000 a case before it is even cleared; its kidney product faces LifePort at 95 percent US share. The number of well-funded rivals has gone from one to four in two years, and the sell-side's own base rate says three-plus well-funded competitors compress EBITDA margins below 20 percent within five years. US lung EVLP penetration has sat near 10 percent for a decade and experts cap it at 10 to 20 percent on cost. Management is a steward, not a founder: late to scale US services, "too slow" on US clinicians' testimony, with a consensus culture that prevents rapid course-correction, an employee net promoter score down from 51 to 27, a finance-director seat shared for seven months with no successor, and a credibility rated medium because regulatory optimism outruns clearance; the North American commercial leadership was let go; surgeons were lost for lack of logistics support. The sell-side that rates it 100 percent Buy has cut FY2026 earnings 28 percent in a year, still models a 347 SEKm heart line for FY2028 from a product with 24 SEKm in its best quarter, and its unanimity with falling estimates is the pattern that carries 40 percent higher subsequent downside volatility; the change-forces report calls it dangerous groupthink. The price has already fallen 25 to 30 percent in a day twice in fifteen months on company news; a 67 percent fall to 163 SEK in 2025 shows what the multiple does. On this reading the 2027 targets (EBITDA margin over 30 percent; abdominal gross margin 70 percent) are missed by a wide margin, the multiple compresses toward the mature medtech set (median 14.9x; a 20 to 23x trough gives 128 to 147 SEK on our earnings), and the shares revisit 145 to 165 SEK (RedEye's bear case; the risks report's 35 to 50 percent downside), which at 25x on our own two-year-forward earnings of 6.4 SEK is exactly where the arithmetic lands (161 SEK, -33 percent). Even without any of that, our own path implies further consensus cuts of 20 to 35 percent, the size of cut that produced the 2025 de-rating, and a plausibly worse below-EBITDA drop-through (amortisation to 210 SEKm in FY2029; tax 25 percent; 33.0m shares) alone cuts FY2029 EPS from 9.5 SEK to 7.8 SEK and the return to 2.9 percent a year at eighteen months (an F) and 13.8 percent a year at three years (a C), taking the 'Modal return' to D and the 'Investment Thesis' to C. The case for the fit is also contestable: this is a clearing story dressed as a demand inflection, with the sector demand only 5 to 7 percent procedure growth and the shares really waiting for a regulatory concern to clear. And the case for a C rather than a D on the 'Investment Case' is that the framework's rules (Goldilocks above 40 percent; a zero dividend; peer problems in a mature set that fits poorly) mark it down for what it is; a company growing 36 percent organic with 129 SEKm of half-year operating cash flow at 30x is a B case with a D risk profile that should net to C.

The record's response, in brief: it concedes the capitalisation point (free cash flow, not EBITDA, is the earnings-quality test; carried into the drop-through sensitivity, the single largest risk to the return), the failure of services for six quarters (our path gives it only a stabilisation), the abdominal margin worse than any broker modelled (our path recovers it to the low 60s, not 70 percent), the regulatory slippage (our path adds a year to the US heart), the unhedged currency, the unanimous consensus 20 to 35 percent above our path, the rebound arithmetic (the clearing setup is the secondary), and that three of the nine D-or-F attributes are calibration. It holds the view because the lung consumables business, 63 percent of revenue at 83 to 85 percent gross margin, growing 53 percent organic in Q2 2026 with 129 SEKm of H1 operating cash flow, is the cash engine that funds every other leg and its growth is acceleration (69 percent after 56 percent) on a sector growing 37 to 65 percent, not a rebound; the capitalised development is a known, finite sum tied to trials that end with approvals; the price at 28x consensus or 37x ours pays for the heart ramp without a premium multiple on top, so the false-friend outcome costs a third to a half and the modal outcome earns the bar, a skew that can be named and sized; and the remaining six D-or-F attributes are defects of this case in particular that a return at the bar cannot absorb. No "covers the enterprise value" claim is made for the thoracic segment, because the files give no thoracic profit line. Where the counter-case wins: lung disposables decelerating below 20 percent while services and abdominal fail to recover; the first test is the Q3 report on 22 October 2026.
triggers: The CE-mark decision on the heart preservation solution: feedback expected during Q3 2026, which ends eight days after the record's date; no file records the outcome. A CE mark by the Q3 report raises the fully cleared heart branch to about 50 percent; a refusal invalidates. Probability by end-2026 about seven in ten on the record's reading.

The US heart PMA: submission "shortly after summer 2026", not announced in the files; review at least twelve months with no deficiencies; approval by end-2027 about one in two; our path assumes 2028. An FDA request for further data or a new trial moves the recommendation to bearish; any regulatory hold or delay over six months is the risks report's re-examination trigger and the record's invalidate level.

The Q3 2026 report on 22 October 2026: the first test of the counter-case and the re-run trigger. Progress needs lung disposables above 30 percent and services no worse, with the CE mark in hand, at or below 230 SEK. Two quarters of lung disposables below 20 percent move to bearish. A Q3 report that cuts FY2027 consensus more than 10 percent or takes the multiple below 25x on consensus is the alarm on the multiple; an approval that lifts FY2028 consensus and the multiple to the two-year median of 33x is the other way.

The entry level: about 230 SEK clears the bar on both horizons on our path; about 200 SEK gives a 25 percent-plus return without a change in the case; 217 SEK and 210 SEK are the A-anchor prices at eighteen months and three years.

The abdominal gross margin: above 62 percent in Q1 2027 with the Gothenburg consolidation done would change our mind toward the fuller recovery; below 60 percent after the consolidation moves to bearish; the consolidation's clean-room validation in Q4 2026 is a named risk.
Services: organic growth positive in Q4 2026 would change our mind; still negative is the alarm.

judgement.heading: Xvivo | Core Investment, sell signal, held under the one-off in/out link | 5.05% of the fund's capital in 3 tranches | outside the order of sale: its tranche rule sells it on release
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** B. Healthcare. Industry RS 46 at the Friday 2 October reading (53 the week before; 46 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** B.5. Medtech, consumables, mature. Sector RS 17 at the 30 September month-end (21 four weeks earlier). Its other companies: Sonova (Stock RS 86), Fresenius (40), Straumann (40), Alcon (23), Coloplast (22), Smith & Nephew (10), and 10 more
- **Cohort:** specialty diagnostic and life-science instruments, including organ preservation. The cohort's relative strength 88 (72 four weeks earlier), 4 companies: Tecan (98, in the Pool), Chemometec (89), Cellavision (72)


**What is going on, and why it matters**

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock fell 9.9% to SEK 214.4; the market's fall explains -0.9%, so its own move was -9.1%, 1.3 times its usual size (about 7.0%). It fell 5.6% on 29 September on about three times its usual volume and 4.5% on 2 October.
  - Over 20 sessions it fell 18.8%, an own move of -16.1%, about its usual size
- **The dated news:** on 28 September the company announced that the US regulator had received its application to approve the Heart Assist Transport system, with a US launch targeted for 2027. The shares fell the next day
  - I cannot tell whether the announcement caused the fall or coincided with it, but the memo's "US heart application not yet submitted" item is now closed and the price did not reward it
- **The sector and cohort:** the cohort's relative strength is 88 (Tecan 98), the sector's 17: Xvivo (Stock RS 37 at the month-end, from 82 at the end of August) has fallen out of a strong cohort, which says the fall is the company's, not the group's
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates 0% and target prices -14% (both -86% at the end of August): the cutting has slowed, but with Stock RS below 50 the negative target-price count still meets the fourth criterion; Sell-side Momentum F

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** held by your one-off link against three whole-holding criteria (Sector RS 17 with Stock RS 37; Stock RS 37 with target-price breadth below zero; relative price 32% below its 52-week high), <u>but all three tranches triggered the 30% fall on 2 October, and that rule is not held back by the link</u>
- **Selling:** the tranches are sold at the first Tuesday session after a close at or above SEK 245.64 (15% above the lowest close since the trigger) or after 63 trading days from 2 October (early January), whichever comes first. The price is 1% below the 30% level (SEK 216.3). No purchase should be spent releasing it
  - If you would rather not wait up to 63 trading days, selling now would be recorded as an overrule of the release rule with your reason
- **Adding:** not allowed and not wanted
- **Its place in the order of sale:** outside it. What would change that: nothing; the tranche rule has taken over
  - What we lose by waiting for the release: the rule's design accepts a further fall in exchange for the chance of a 15% bounce, which I put below even with the analysts negative and the stock falling at its usual pace, so the base case is the 63rd day in early January
    - The third-quarter report on 22 October and the European heart decision are both inside the window

**What we could lose:** nothing to the 30% level, which is above the price; the position's further fall is open-ended until the release (a 10% fall from here costs about 0.5% of capital)

**Experiment: which stocks Xvivo's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)

- **Camurus** (same country of listing): 0.29 and 0.19, weak
- **Bonesupport** (same country of listing): 0.26 and 0.23, weak
- **Fastighets Balder** (same country of listing): 0.29 and 0.13, weak
- **Ambu** (same sector): 0.30 and 0.11, weak
- **My reading:** its moves are mostly its own, as a company with one proven engine and a regulator holding the key should be

**The Investment Analyst's memo (digest of 22 September at SEK 240; memo republished 1 October)**

- **Decided:** neutral; park, pending two dated events: the European decision on the heart preservation solution and the third-quarter report on 22 October; conviction a working hypothesis; gates all C
- **Must happen:** a European mark in hand and a third-quarter report with lung disposables growing above 30% and services no worse, at a price at or below SEK 230; or any price below about SEK 200 without a change in the case
- **Main risk:** a science company whose 2026 acceleration is a rebound from a destocked 2025, dressed up by capitalised development; an FDA request for further heart data
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** below our bar at SEK 240; clears it on both horizons below about SEK 230, and a 25%-plus return below about SEK 200
- **Next test:** the third-quarter report on 22 October; the European decision

**My judgement:** bearish on the position, medium conviction: the stock has fallen out of a strong cohort on its own account, the analysts are negative, and the tranche rule has already decided the exit; let the rule run and do not spend a purchase on it.

- **Counter-case:** the price (SEK 214) is now below the memo's entry level (SEK 230) and near the SEK 200 at which the memo sees a 25%-plus return; the US application is filed
  - If the European mark arrives with a strong lung print on 22 October, the 15% bounce that releases the tranches would sell the holding into the very news the memo waited for

**What would change my view:** a close at or above SEK 245.64 (release); the 22 October report (lung disposables above 30%); the European decision; the 63rd trading day in early January
